text:
alex.s: FYI customer acme-corp is seeing intermittent 504s and then NXDOMAIN for their private service endpoint `api.internal.acme` from prod VPC only. Started ~2h after hosted-zone consolidation.
customer-ops: Affects only prod VPC subnets (10.0.32/20). Dev/staging fine. Impacting healthchecks and causing failovers.
mira.support: Can you paste a failing `dig` from a pod in the affected subnet and the VPC id? Also any recent infra changes besides the consolidation?
alex.s: VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d. Dig from a pod: ```; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> api.internal.acme @127.0.0.53 +short ;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345```
sam.dns: Can you check node-local-dns / CoreDNS pods and /etc/resolv.conf on a failing node? NXDOMAIN + only in prod often points to resolver rule or on-prem forwarder returning NXDOMAIN or stale node-local cache.
jordan-sre: Hosted-zone consolidation pushed 2h ago (consolidation/2026-03-17). Also noticed a new resolver rule created in shared-services account yesterday. Could be a forwarder intercepting `internal.acme`.
alex.s: Checked node-local: pods healthy. `cat /etc/resolv.conf` in pod shows `nameserver 169.254.20.10` (node-local). `kubectl -n kube-system get ds node-local-dns` shows 3/3.
mira.support: Ok. Can you run these from a failing node/pod: 1) `dig api.internal.acme @169.254.20.10 +trace` 2) `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters Name=CreatorRequestId,Values=consolidation*` 3) `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "internal.acme."` ?
alex.s: Paste outputs: ```; trace to 169.254.20.10 ... ;; ->>HEADER<<- status: NXDOMAIN ... aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules -> RuleId: rslvr-xyz forwarding to 10.10.10.5 (onprem) aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name -> HostedZones: internal.acme. (private, account: acct-consolidated)```
sam.dns: Aha — resolver rule in shared-services forwards `internal.acme` to on-prem resolver 10.10.10.5. On-prem doesn't have the new consolidated records for that tenant, so it returns NXDOMAIN. Some VPCs are associated with that rule (probably prod), others not.
mira.support: That explains selective failure. Two mitigation paths: 1) disassociate the forwarding resolver rule from the affected prod VPC(s) so they use Route53 private hosted zone locally, 2) update on-prem forwarder/zone with the consolidated records. Which can we do now?
jordan-sre: We should disassociate first to restore service ASAP, then sync on-prem. I'll disassociate for vpc-0a1b2c3d now. @eng-oncall-bot kicking deploy/infra change window request.
eng-oncall-bot: infra-change-request: user=jordan-sre action=disassociate-resolver-rule resource=rslvr-xyz target=vpc-0a1b2c3d time=2419007920 status=approved
jordan-sre: Disassociated rule rslvr-xyz from vpc-0a1b2c3d. Please flush caches: restart node-local-dns pods or `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart ds/node-local-dns`.
alex.s: Restarted node-local-dns pods, waited TTL. Re-ran dig: ```api.internal.acme. 60 IN A 10.0.40.12``` Customer confirms service healthy again, no more 504s.
mira.support: Great. Root cause: shared-services resolver rule forwarded consolidated namespace to on-prem without having the new tenant records, causing NXDOMAIN for VPCs associated with that rule. Action items: - remove unintended VPC associations for forwarding rules (shared-services) - add a pre-check in consolidation runbook to detect resolver-rule overlaps - coordinate on-prem zone sync for consolidated tenants.
customer-ops: Customer notified, they confirmed recovery. Thanks everyone. :tada:
alex.s: Marking resolved, will follow up with runbook PR to avoid recurrence.
